report: Who should I contact to make a complaint about how my maintenance issue was handled?
reply: To make a complaint about how your maintenance issue was handled, you should contact your building manager. Please include the original report and any job number you were provided.

sections.title: Contacting staff and raising complaints
sections.text: Use your residence's published contact details. If reception is closed, use the published out-of-hours contact. For an unresolved maintenance complaint, contact your building manager with the original report and any job number.

sections.title: Urgent hazards
sections.text: Contact the duty team promptly about loss of power to the whole flat, signs of electrical danger, a dark shared stairwell, unsafe shared routes, broken glass on a shared route, structural danger or someone trapped in a lift. A single fitting that stops working without signs of danger can usually be reviewed as a repair. Say what you can see and which area is affected.

report: What is the target for getting my radiator fixed, and is that a guaranteed completion time?
reply: The recorded target for job 205 is noon UTC on 12 November 2026. That is a repair target, not a guaranteed completion time.

sections.title: Repair targets
sections.text:
For fixed lighting, another working fixed light in the same room means P3 with a 7 day target. If no fixed light works in that room, use P2 with a 1 day target from when that fact was first confirmed. A torch, desk lamp or working light in another room does not count. Staff may ask you to confirm whether a second fixed light works.

Verified heating faults have a P2, 2 day target. Verified appliance faults have a P3, 7 day target. These targets guide repairs. The confirmed job record shows the target for your repair.
